45	- **THE HARNESS'S CAPTURE ACTION IS `captureClient` + `path`; `capture` + `name` FAILS SILENTLY (R117, load-bearing, cost 3 round-trips).** A command whose `action` matches nothing **hits the fallback with no error**: `harness/command.json` updates, the app logs nothing new, and **no PNG appears anywhere**. The tell is the log line `[UIReview] native app client capture <path> true` — if it is absent, nothing was written. **Always grep that line after a capture, and `ls` the file.** (R064 said the fallback is silent; this is the round that paid for it.)
46	- **THE REFERENCE ITSELF CAN SPEND TWO TONES ON ONE SEMANTIC COLOUR (R117, load-bearing).** Its mini-month today disc is **`(207,51,35)`** but its 9:41 now-pill is **`(235,76,70)`** — both are "today red". macOS renders systemRed through *vibrancy* in the sidebar and flat in the toolbar. ⇒ **When a reference tone is taken from a vibrant surface, it is not a token value; it is a render.** Sample the same semantic colour on a *flat* surface in the same screenshot before proposing a literal. **(Corollary: a single screenshot can contain two renderings of one token — never derive a token from one sample.)**
47	- **A SIZE LITERAL BEATS A REF MEASUREMENT, BUT THE MEASUREMENT MUST BE RECORDED BESIDE IT (R115/R117, load-bearing).** M04 says **18–20**; the ref is **15 at 1:1** and **17.2–17.3** scaled. We shipped **18** and wrote both numbers down. **The clause and the ref disagree; the clause wins; the ref number stays in the record so a later ruling can revisit it.**
48	- **A RING AND A DIGIT THAT SHARE ONE TOKEN FUSE INTO ONE READING (R116, load-bearing).** R115 read our selection as a ring peaking `(0,136,255)` with the digit `(63,63,66)`, "32 px, the cell's modal non-plane tone". The deleted source shows why that is a **two-tone misidentification**: the digit's colour *was* `root.tahoe.accent`, i.e. **the same `(0,136,255)` as the border**, and the tone it took for the digit is dark `selectionFill` = **63**, the **ring's interior fill**. ⇒ **Before calling a value "the digit", check the source for the digit's colour and the outline's colour: if they are one token, a threshold ladder cannot separate them and a ×6 zoom still cannot.**
49	- **THE MINI MONTH'S GRID IS MONTH-INDEPENDENT (R115/R117, load-bearing).** The six date-band tops are **561/582/603/624/645/666** — identical in the Apr-2026 capture and the Oct-2026 one — and the disc overhangs its 9-row band. **R117: a disc SIZE change did not move a single band** (col-0 starts still 545/561/582/603/624/645/666/688), because the disc is `anchors.centerIn` a fixed cell. ⇒ a mini-month reading taken on one month holds for any month, **and a disc geometry change is band-neutral by construction.**
50	- **A 9-ROW GLYPH INSIDE A DISC IS NOT LEGIBLE ENOUGH TO CARRY A TONE CLAIM (R115, load-bearing).** R112/R114 read the selection disc's digit as "the ordinary text tone" at 1:1; the **×6 zoom** separated a 63-tone fill from a 216-tone glyph. **Ring/disc interiors need a zoom before any tone claim** — a threshold that separates the ring from the plane will not separate the digit from the ring.
51	- **A DISC'S RIM NEEDS AN ENVELOPE, NOT A TONE TOLERANCE, AND THE ENVELOPE MUST BE ROW-BOUNDED (R117).** A ±7 tolerance on the gray tone reads the disc as **16 wide**, because the rim blends toward the 228 plane within 1 px; a saturated-red threshold reads the SAME 18 px disc as 18. **The pair is the instrument:** measure both discs with one criterion (`sum(px) < 3*228 − 60`) and report their equality, never an absolute box from a single tolerance. **And keep the row range inside the disc's own cell** — an envelope spanning several rows picks up the neighbouring dates' glyphs (R117 read a 40-row "disc" that way before clamping).
52	- **THE SIDEBAR'S 1 px RIM AT x220 EXISTS ON BOTH LEGS (R114, load-bearing).** Dark `(53,53,53)` at x220 with the plane 40 at x219; light `(224,224,224)` with the plane 228. **A whole-sidebar ink scan must stop at x219.**
53	- **THE MINI MONTH HAS NO FILL OF ITS OWN (R114, load-bearing).** The block's field IS the sidebar plane ((40,40,40) dark / 228 light, the dominant tone in **every** row), so **M01's 12 / 12 margins are arithmetic, not tonal**: they follow from `cellWidth 196/7 = 28.0` and the column centres 26.0 + 28.0i (⇒ cells 12..208 in a 220 px sidebar). The same is true on light.
54	- **A BAND SCAN ON A DISC-BEARING ROW MUST BE DISC-FREE (R114).** The disc extends above and below the 9-row text band, so a full-width scan of the selected row reads wider than a disc-free scan. **R117: at 18 px the disc extends 4–5 px above and 2–3 below the 603..611 band** — a wider overhang than R114's 15 px disc gave, so a band scan on the disc row is now MORE polluted, not less.
55	- **A PIXEL RUN p..q IS THE HALF-OPEN INTERVAL [p, q+1) — ITS CENTRE IS (p+q+1)/2 (R112, load-bearing calibration).** **R117 used it to land both disc centres exactly on `12 + 28c + 14`: 110.0 and 166.0.** The inclusive form `(p+q)/2` would have shifted them to 109.5 / 165.5 and read as a misalignment that is not there. A GAP written as `line - last_ink_pixel` is the inclusive form and reads 1 larger than the continuous gap — **state which form a gap came from.**
56	- **THE PAIR, NOT THE BOX, IS THE INSTRUMENT ON A DARK LEG (R114).** An ink box reads ±1 px differently against a 40 plane than against 228, so a dark-leg fidelity claim must rest on a **pair comparison** — arrow vs arrow, dark vs light, at two thresholds — never on an absolute box edge. **R116/R117 applied the same instrument on one leg: the two discs measure equal to the pixel.**
57	- **A DARK `gridLine` COMPOSITES, A LIGHT ONE DOES NOT (R113, load-bearing).** The dark separators read **59** over the weekday field 30 and **65** over the weekend tint 37 — one token, `white@0.13`, two backdrops. The light `#EDEDED` is opaque and reads 237 everywhere. ⇒ **"all separators share one tone" is a light-leg fact.**
58	- **A RULE ROW'S GUTTER SEGMENT IS THE LABEL, NEVER A LINE (R111, load-bearing).** The hour/half-hour rules span **x272..x1099** only — the grid's left edge to the window's last pixel. In a rule row the only non-white pixels left of x272 are the gutter label's own ink (`238..264`).
59	- **A CLIPPED LABEL BAND IS STILL AN ALIGNMENT READING IF ITS INK X-EXTENT MATCHES ITS SIBLINGS (R111).**
60	- **THE HOUR LABELS SCROLL WITH THE GRID (R111, load-bearing).** At `contentY 240` the top tick is hour 6 at screen y234 and the label bands sit at 274/314/.../674 — a gutter scan must be indexed by **tick**, not by absolute hour.
61	- **EXPANDED-SIDEBAR T03 GEOMETRY, MEASURED (R111).** Gutter **221..272**; label ink **x238..264**, right gap **8** to the grid line at 272; separators **1 px 237** at **272/391/510/629/748/867** (**pitch 119**); weekend tint **249** right of the x867 separator. Label band = **9 rows**, font 11.

63	- **`opacity: 0.5` ON A COMPLETED ITEM RE-CREATES THE EXACT DEFECT R109 FIXED (R109, load-bearing).** `CalendarScheduleView.qml:550` still fades a completed chip with item `opacity`. **No completed all-day item exists in the fixture. Recorded, not fixed.**
64	- **A TRANSLUCENT CHIP CANNOT BE JOINED BY OVERLAP (R108, load-bearing).** A join must be an opaque pre-blend. R109's reach = 3 px measured, 4 px shipped.
65	- **THE JOINT'S 3 px IS ONE PIXEL OF SLACK IN THREE PIECES (R108, load-bearing).** A column is **119.0 px** (833/7) and draws its own separator as its **FIRST** pixel; the chips sit inset 1 ⇒ a chip is **116 px inside a 119 px column**.
66	- **ONLY A LEFT-EXTENSION CAN HIDE A RULE (R108, load-bearing).** A right-extension can never cover the neighbour's rule; the neighbour's own chip, extending **left**, can.
67	- **A CONTINUATION IS A DATE FACT; A COLUMN IS A PLACE (R109, load-bearing).** `allDayContinues()` is pure date arithmetic; **gate the reach on `allDayColumn.index > 0`.**
68	- **THE ALL-DAY BAND IS CONTENT-SIZED WITH A ONE-ROW FLOOR (R106, load-bearing).** `allDayBandRows = clamp(maxItemsAcrossThe7Columns, 1, 3)`: **26 px** all-day-empty, **76** on the 3-row week. **`allDayMaxRows` and `allDayBandRows` must stay separate variables.**
69	- **OUR WEEKS START MONDAY, AND AN EXPANDED SIDEBAR SHIFTS THE DAY COLUMNS (R106, load-bearing).** Expanded: gutter **221..272**, separators at **272/391/510/629/748/867/986** — **pitch 119**. So **`x=577` is the 3rd day column; Thursday is 629..747 (x~690)**. **R115 note: the reference's mini month headers read `S M T W T F S` (Sunday-first) where ours read `一二三四五六日` (Monday-first) — an unfiled heading divergence. M02's clauses are unaffected.**
70	- **AN ALL-DAY-EMPTY WEEK STILL SHOWS A 26 px BAND (R106, extrapolation).** The spec says "min about 28", so the band has a floor rather than a hide.
71	- **THE REF'S SIDEBAR IS 192 px WIDE — "243px sidebar" WAS A CONFLATION (R105, load-bearing).** The 237-plane ends at **x=191**; the white hour gutter runs **192..243** and the first *day column* starts at **243**. ⇒ the reference's **main region is 192..813, centre 502.5** — and its segment's rim centre is **502.0**. **R063–R104 carried the wrong denominator ⇒ any ref-centredness number derived from "grid 243..812" must be recomputed.**
72	- **A CENTRED-IN-REGION SEGMENT IS −0.5 px ON BOTH SIDES, AND THAT IS THE CONVENTION (R105, load-bearing).**
73	- **A CAPSULE'S OUTER RADIUS IS MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN INNER ELEMENT, NEVER IN ABSOLUTE PX (R104, load-bearing).**
74	- **AN ARC-ONLY FIT CANNOT SEPARATE r FROM y0 AND IS THEREFORE NOT AN ABSOLUTE INSTRUMENT (R104, load-bearing).** **Report the bound (11–13.5), not a point.**
75	- **A PILL'S HORIZONTAL PADDING IS MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN SLOT, AND THE SLOTS OF A SEGMENTED CONTROL TILE (R102, load-bearing; R103).** **R103: the rule applies to both sides or the comparison is void. Correct ref slot = (228−4)/4 = 56.0.**
76	- **A WHOLE-CONTROL WIDTH CAN BE A SPEC LITERAL THAT OVERRIDES THE REFERENCE (R103, load-bearing).** **L03 fixes 180–210 ⇒ a 3-label control can never match a 4-label reference's pill width.**
77	- **WORD CENTRES BEAT CONTROL EDGES FOR A PITCH (R103, load-bearing).**
78	- **THE REFERENCE'S SEGMENTED CONTROL AND OURS SHARE ONE RADIUS TOKEN (R101–R104).** Ref lens **r ≈ 11.5 on h 24 (0.48)**; ref track **r ≈ 13.4–13.5**; ours **0.48 on both**.
79	- **A RADIUS IS MEASURED 1:1 AGAINST A SAME-HEIGHT ELEMENT, AND THE METHOD MUST RECOVER A KNOWN TOKEN FIRST (R101, load-bearing).** **threshold = the midpoint of THAT IMAGE's own two constants**; **only when the profile is monotone across the edge. R104: prefer the *within-image* track-vs-lens profile.**
80	- **A WHOLE-PAGE `ImageChops.difference` WITH A PER-ROW DIFF COUNT IS STILL THE CHEAPEST CONTAINMENT PROOF (R088).** Threshold **>6 RGB-sum**. **R109 used it to prove the `index > 0` guard is invisible.**
81	- **NEVER SCALE A REF *TYPE* ELEMENT BY THE WINDOW RATIO — FIND A SAME-CLASS INK IN BOTH IMAGES FIRST (R086).**
82	- **MEASURING A CORNER, A JOINT, A STRIPE, A BORDER OR AN INK (R075–R117).** Corner: per-row **fill-start inset** (body mode, R098; **interior rows, indexed from the first counted row, validated on a known token — R101/R102**; **R103: only on a monotone edge**; **R104: on a 250-on-255 fill use the rim's argmin core, and compare the outer element against the inner one in the SAME image**). Joint: per-row **`!= white` envelope**; **R107: a shared *horizontal* edge is separator-tone + the very next row's tone; R108: a shared *vertical* edge is the pair of fill edges plus whatever sits between them, and a JOIN must be read as an absolute tone against the fill; R109: after the join, the acceptance is "the fill envelope is unbroken and contains no 255 and no rule tone".** Stripe: a saturated run whose **width is constant over the chip's full height**. Border: **monotonicity of a raw profile across an edge that abuts no rule**. Ink: the **per-channel coverage agreement test PLUS the channel-gap argument**; cross-capture: **top-5 %-coverage mean** and **`n<100`**; **R115: a glyph inside a disc needs a ×6 zoom**; **R116: and if the glyph and its outline share one token, even the zoom needs the source**; **R117: a *disc* needs an ENVELOPE under one criterion for both members of the pair, row-bounded to its own cell — a per-tone tolerance reads the same disc 2 px narrow.** **Pitch: word centres, not edges (R103).**
83	- **HARNESS / COMMAND / TOKEN RULES.**
84	  **THE CAPTURE ACTION IS `captureClient` + `path` (R117).** `capture` + `name` matches no `action` and **silently hits the fallback**: no PNG, no log line. Verify with `grep "native app client capture" live-runtime-vm.log` **and** `ls` the file. **A `captureClient` RETURN OF `false` MEANS A NESTED RELATIVE PATH AND THE PNG IS SILENTLY NOT WRITTEN (R075)** — pass a **flat filename**. **Pillow crops need ABSOLUTE paths** — the shell CWD moves between calls. **R107: our PNGs are written at zlib level 0 — three different captures share a byte size, so compare `md5sum`, never the size.**
85	  **THE LAUNCHER REFUSES WHEN A LIVED INSTANCE IS ALIVE (R079), AND `>/dev/null` HIDES IT.** `start-review-vm.sh` exits **1** with `Owned review instance still running: <pid>`. **ALWAYS `kill -0 $(cat live-app.pid)` FIRST: if the leg you need is already alive, the capture is FREE** (R114/R115 both took that path). **R116/R117: a REBUILT binary needs kill + relaunch — a live instance keeps running the OLD resources, theme fixed at launch — so a source change always costs the full cycle (kill `live-app.pid` → `nohup ./start-review-vm.sh light|dark &` → `sleep 40` → `python3 review-command.py '<json list>'` → grep `capture ... true`).**
86	  **`review-command.py` IS NOT EXECUTABLE — always `python3 review-command.py`.** It takes **ONE argv that is a JSON list**, bumps `sequence` from the file's own last value, writes **in place** (never `os.replace`), sleeps 0.6 s between commands.
87	  **HARNESS COMMAND FORM IS FLAT (R064).** `harness/Main.qml` matches `command.action` only; a command with no `action` **silently hits the fallback**. Include `resize 1100x692`; the app starts in `--view week --date 2026-10-15` **with the sidebar COLLAPSED** (`{"action":"sidebar","expanded":true}` expands it; `{"action":"date","date":"YYYY-MM-DD"}` re-dates). Only `date`/`position`/`wheel`/`flick`/`stop`/`openItem{kind,titleContains}`/`windowWheel`/`captureClient` are available: **`hovered`/`pressed` chrome cannot be driven, and a static screenshot can never settle an animation.**
88	  **Compositing (R077/R080/R088/R097/R099/R101–R109/R115/R116/R117).** **A composite (a 1:1 strip above/beside a 2–6× zoom) answers "overall form + local detail" in ONE image read**, and **labelling the rows (`ImageDraw.text`) is what makes it self-describing.** **`LANCZOS` for a ×1.8 upscale of a ref crop; `NEAREST` when the point is pixel structure.** **Captions go on the FINAL canvas at 1x — text drawn *before* an ×N upscale is illegible, and the canvas height must include the caption block.** **R109: side-by-side panel captions collide even at 615 px of canvas — stack caption LINES, one per panel, at full width. R116: three panels side by side (ref 192 + ours 220 + zoom 612) fit in `W = 1080` with a single full-width caption line at the foot.
